title: Scanner-to-NIST candidate corpus
description: A ranked review queue produced outside this repo: for each scanner check, the NIST SP 800-53 controls a scoring harness proposes, with the score that ordered them. A candidate is a suggestion awaiting human adjudication and confers no mapping authority. Field names follow the upstream artifact wherever it already carries the field, so ingestion needs no wholesale renaming; the three the contract adds or renames are recorded in provenance.md.
$comment: This document states the shape. Rules it cannot express — that a control id exists at the declared revision, that one revision explains the whole candidate set, that a scanner version is concrete — live in the validators (go/controlmapping/validate.go and src/control-mapping/index.ts), and go/controlmapping/testdata/candidate-validation-cases.json is the worked case table both read. A test in each language asserts every property required here is in fact enforced by the validator, so the two cannot drift.

schema.description: Schema literal. Refused outright when it is anything else, before the rest of the document is trusted.

catalog.description: The NIST catalog the scores were computed against.

source.description: Human-readable catalog name. Prose only — revision is the field validated against.

revision.description: The SP 800-53 revision the corpus was indexed against. Every candidate control id must exist at this revision. A corpus whose ids span revisions is refused regardless of what this declares, because a mixed catalog skews every score computed over it.

pinned_commit.description: Commit of the catalog source the harness read, so the scores can be re-derived.

scanner.description: The tool whose check catalog this corpus maps.

name.description: Scanner name, which keys the published mapping.

version.description: The concrete scanner release scored. An image reference is accepted and its tag judged; a floating tag such as latest is refused, because the set of checks scored would be unknowable. Scanners that stamp their own version into their reports let a converter cross-check this at convert time.

checks.description: Count of checks in the scanner's catalog, carried for provenance.

method.description: Upstream's account of how the scores were produced. Carried uninterpreted; this repo draws no conclusion from it.

checks.description: Candidates keyed by scanner check id. An empty object is an upstream build failure, not an empty import.

query_name.description: The check's name in the scanner's own catalog.

cwe.description: CWE the scanner associates with the check, when it names one.

category.description: The scanner's own category for the check.

candidates.description: Proposed controls in rank order. A check with nothing to propose must be absent rather than present and empty, so adjudication cannot read it as reviewed-and-rejected.

control.description: The proposed control, at any granularity the catalog defines: a family-level control (AU-2, SA-15), an enhancement (SA-10.4), or a statement sub-part (AU-2 a, SA-4.3 (a)). A bare family code (AU) is not a control and is refused, because it cannot be a tags.nist value. Enhancements written with a dot are translated to NIST's parenthesised spelling on ingest, and the id must then normalize and exist at the declared revision.

control_title.description: The control's title as the harness read it from the catalog.

score.description: Rank score within this check, normalised to 0..1. Absent is refused rather than read as 0.0.

matched_on.description: Which catalog text fields the match drew on.
